answer: Decentralized trust-graph routing curbs Sybil attacks by bounding credit flow along verified peer connections. In this model, established agents cannot harbor unvetted identities without staking their own credit capacity. Whether coordinating sensors across a coastal reef or an arctic tundra station, an adversary must expend scarce historical capital and vouching trust per node. However, this creates strict network silos that disadvantage newly initialized, legitimate agents.
